bill.title: An Act amending the act of April 6, 1951 (P.L.69, No.20), known as The Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951, in recovery of possession, further providing for hearing, judgment, writ of possession and payment of rent by tenant.

posted_text:
🔑 PA HB 2023 — Landlord-Tenant Disputes Now Consider Extreme Weather

This bill changes how Pennsylvania courts handle evictions.

If extreme weather – like freezing temperatures, winter storms, hurricanes, or excessive heat – makes it difficult to enforce a writ of possession, the judge can temporarily stop the eviction.

This pause applies specifically to tenants receiving assistance through programs like Medicaid, SNAP, SSI, or the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program.

The court must complete the eviction within five days after the weather improves.

The law will take effect 60 days from passage.

Oct. 26, 2026: Referred to Urban Affairs & Housing.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.palegis.us/legislation/bills/2025/hb2023
